name: Celeste

scale.why: Madeline's hitbox is 11 px tall (Player.cs: normalHitbox 8 x 11), scaled to 1.8 m: 0.1636 m/px. A 2D platformer: compare ratios (dash / run) more than raw speeds

gravity.note: halved near the apex while jump is held (HalfGravThreshold 40) (x6.6942 is outside the editor's 0.1..3 range: applying it clamps.)

jump.note: held for up to 0.2 s while jump is held (VarJumpTime), so jumps are much higher than v^2/2g

dash_exit_min.note: the speed a dash ends at (Quark's exit is at least 11 m/s)

dash_charges.note: one dash, refilled on landing (two with the second crystal heart power-up)

super_dash_jump.note: the hyper (a super jump out of a crouched dash) jumps at half the jump speed: Quark's super dash hop started at the same 0.5 until 1.18.28 raised it to 0.866

superJumpSpeed.note: the super (dash jump) horizontal speed: 2.89 x run (Quark's dash jump leaves at the 24 m/s burst, 2.53 x)

hyperSpeed.note: the hyper: 325 px/s, 3.6 x run (Quark's super dash: carried speed + 5 m/s)

jumpHeight.source: derived from JumpSpeed, VarJumpTime, Gravity, HalfGravThreshold
jumpHeight.note: about 28 px (21 px held + 7 px coasting) = 2.5 x her height; Quark: 1.22 m = 0.68 x

extras: super / hyper / wavedash (dash techs Quark's dash jump and super dash are modelled on)
notes: Celeste's Player.cs was published by its developers. A 2D game: its gravity and jumps are far beyond a shooter's; the dash numbers are the useful comparison.
